_comment: Adversarial corpus for the fact-boundary validator (PRD §10.2, M3).
Written during M0, deliberately BEFORE the validator exists, so the
detectors are graded against a target they did not author.
'block' cases are fabrications that must never reach a form.
'pass' cases are honest text that must NOT be blocked — false positives
are their own failure. A validator that rejects true statements gets
switched off, and then it protects nobody.

cases.text: AWS Certified Solutions Architect with five years of cloud experience.
cases.why: Holds Cloud Practitioner, not Solutions Architect. Certifications are binary and verifiable.

cases.text: AWS Certified Developer, with hands-on Docker experience.
cases.why: A different AWS certification is still one they do not hold.

cases.text: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner with production Docker experience.
cases.why: Exactly the credential on file, plus an allowed skill.

cases.text: I am a certified cloud professional.
cases.why: Unspecific certification language still asserts a credential.

cases.text: Built REST services in Django and Spring Boot.
cases.why: Django and Spring Boot are not in the boundary; FastAPI is.

cases.text: Wrote high-performance data pipelines in Rust and Go.
cases.why: Neither language is evidenced anywhere in the Brain.

cases.text: Built REST services in Python with FastAPI, backed by PostgreSQL.
cases.why: Every technology named is in the boundary.

cases.text: My Docker experience should transfer well to your Kubernetes stack.
cases.why: Names an unowned technology as the employer's, not as the candidate's experience. PRD §10.2 allows adjacent tech as context.

cases.text: Operated production Kubernetes clusters at scale.
cases.why: The same technology, now claimed as experience. This is the line.

cases.text: Senior Engineer at Google, leading the payments platform.
cases.why: Employer not in preserved_orgs.

cases.text: Backend engineer at Northwind Systems, owning the ingestion service.
cases.why: Employer is on file.

cases.text: MIT graduate with a focus on distributed systems.
cases.why: Institution not in preserved_institutions.

cases.text: Computer science graduate of the University of Dhaka.
cases.why: Institution is on file.

cases.text: I built OpenTelemetry-Lite, a tracing library used by 200 companies.
cases.why: Project does not exist in the Brain.

cases.text: I built Haru, a local-first agent that fills forms from a personal record.
cases.why: Project is on file.

cases.text: Reduced infrastructure costs by 85% in the first quarter.
cases.why: Not in real_metrics. Invented numbers are the most persuasive fabrication and the easiest to check.

cases.text: Made query performance 400% faster.
cases.why: The verified metric is 40% faster. Inflation of a real number is still fabrication.

cases.text: Cut query latency, making the ingestion path 40% faster.
cases.why: Uses a verified metric verbatim.

cases.text: Sustained 12000 rows/sec through the ingestion pipeline.
cases.why: Verified metric, different sentence. Rephrasing is allowed; the number is not changed.

cases.text: I led a team of 15 engineers on this project.
cases.why: Real metric says 3 person team.

cases.text:
Here is the revised cover letter:

Dear Hiring Manager, I am writing to apply.
cases.why: Model preamble inside the deliverable. Pure output corruption.

cases.text: I apologize for the error. Built the ingestion service in Python.
cases.why: Model talking to itself.

cases.text: Note: I have updated this answer per your feedback.
cases.why: Meta-commentary addressed to the operator, not the reader.

cases.text: I note that your team is rebuilding its ingestion pipeline.
cases.why: Contains the word 'note' in an ordinary sentence. Must not trip the leak detector.

cases.text: I am a passionate, detail-oriented self-starter with a proven track record of spearheading robust, cutting-edge solutions.
cases.why: Blocking in strict mode only.

cases.text: I am a passionate, detail-oriented self-starter with a proven track record.
cases.why: Clichés warn but do not block in normal mode. Result carries warnings; passed stays true.

cases.text: I spent two years on ingestion at Northwind Systems and want to keep working on data infrastructure.
cases.why: Plain, specific, honest. The target register.

cases.text: Built services in Python.
cases.why: With no confirmed facts nothing may be claimed at all. An empty boundary means 'cannot generate yet', not 'no limits'.

cases.text: Deep experience with python, postgres and DOCKER.
cases.why: Casing and spelling variants of owned skills must not be treated as fabrication.

cases.text: I have not worked with Kubernetes, though I have used Docker in production.
cases.why: Explicitly disclaims an unowned skill. Blocking this would punish honesty — the worst possible false positive.
